summary: Windows Sysmon log rotation overlap prevents Intune diagnostic bundle upload
description:
Issue summary:
On a subset of Windows laptops the Intune/Redwood diagnostic agent fails to upload full diagnostic bundles when Sysmon continuous logs rotate. The agent reports partial bundle generation and upload attempts fail with 500-level errors from the diagnostics intake service.

Impact:
- Affects fleet health telemetry for some end-user devices returning from depot/repair or after image refresh.
- Prevents collection of full crash/trace bundles for troubleshooting, delaying incident resolution.
- Estimated ~0.4% of daily checkins in us-east show the pattern (sampling).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, Windows 10/11 corporate images, Intune-managed devices
- Observed primarily on devices with high-frequency Sysmon config (continuous: true) and aggressive circular file rotation (Sysmon config shipped via configmgr).

Steps to reproduce (observed in lab):
1) Provision device with corporate image + Sysmon enabled with continuous logging and file rotation every 50MB.
2) Boot device and run workload to generate high-volume events (VM start/stop, network scans).
3) Trigger Intune diagnostic upload via Company Portal > "Collect diagnostics".
4) Observe diagnostic-agent logs: partial bundle ZIP produced, upload fails with 500 from diagnostics-intake, then agent retries, later produces a smaller bundle after Sysmon file rollover.

Observed behavior:
- diagnostics-agent.log shows: "bundle generation complete (files: 1/3)" then HTTP 500 from diagnostics-intake.service.redwood.internal
- Sysmon logs are rotated mid-bundle creation; file handles are re-opened by sysmon and timestamp overlap leads to an inconsistent file size reported to the zipping routine.
- Final uploaded bundle is missing the largest Sysmon chunk.

Expected behavior:
- Diagnostics agent should either snapshot consistent file handles for zipping or gracefully detect rotation and retry bundling so the full Sysmon set is included.

Logs/Artifacts:
- diagnostics-agent.log excerpts (attached to ticket).
- sysmon-config.xml (corporate rotation policy) referenced in investigation.
- example partial bundles (sha256s included in investigation notes).

Notes:
- Customer-impacting but small subset of fleet; appears correlated with aggressive Sysmon rotation + high event rate (VM dev images, telemetry-heavy users).

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: race between Sysmon rotation (truncate + reopen) and diagnostics-agent file enumeration leads to corrupted/partial bundles.
Reproduced in lab: high-frequency event generator + size-based Sysmon rotation reproduced missing chunk in 7/10 runs.

Diagnostics-agent currently enumerates path, then streams files into ZIP without re-checking sizes or file handles after open. When Sysmon truncates and reopens, ZIP stream may end before the new write completes.
Workaround tested: pause Sysmon service before running collection -> bundles contain full Sysmon logs (not acceptable for end-users, but verifies root cause).
Intake 500s were sometimes observed concurrently due to autoscaling cold starts; added temporary retry policy in front of diagnostics-intake to reduce noise while agent fix rolls out.
Related: INT-527350 shows a different diagnostic upload failure path after ssd replace; likely unrelated but useful for triage history.
resolution: In-progress fix: diagnostics-agent PR implements file-handle sanity checks and a small retry loop when file sizes change between list and read. Patch merged to staging and smoke-tested on the lab fleet (10 devices) with 10/10 successful full bundles. Plan: staged rollout to prod-us-east (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 48 hours assuming no regressions. Follow-up: update Sysmon corporate config guidance to avoid overly aggressive rotation on high-telemetry dev images and add instrumentation to detect partial bundles and surface them in Console. Closing notes and formal postmortem will be added to linked Confluence page after full rollout.
